pro_course_detail.title: Level One
pro_course_detail.description:
Themes:
1. Working together to learn a new language. (Present tense of to be, articles)
2. Team building (Present simple 1, plurals and there is and there are)
3. Caring of the enviroment (Present simple 2, and to have)
4. Equality the roles of men women (Present continuous, can and can't, 's for possession)
5. Dental health (Countables/Uncountables, much/many, some/any, like+gerund)
6. World religions (Past simple 1, adverbs of frequency)
7. Road safety (Past simple 2, irregular past verbs)
8. Animal Care (Comparatives, must for obligation and prohibition)
9. Understanding differences between countries (Superlatives, going to)
10. Review.

pro_course_detail.title: Level Two
pro_course_detail.description:
1. New Vocabulary (Hobbies, interests, Adjectives to describe people, clothes)
2. Consumer education (Comparatives and superlatives)
3. Safety rules (Revision of past simple, past continuous)
4. Music and eating (Present perfect for experiences, past participles)
5. Health (Countables/Uncountables, should for suggestions and recommendations)
6. Movies (Adverbs of manner)
7. International signs (Going to, first conditional)
8. Environmental Issues (Modal verbs, have to)
9. Literature (Present passive, verb and preposition)
10. Read a newspaper articles

pro_course_detail.title: Level Three
pro_course_detail.description:
1. Racial Tolerance (Talking about possibility and obligation)
2. The environment literature poetry. Traditional music (Talking about likes and dislikes)
3. Talking about future and feeling (Suffixes and prepositions of place, signs and notices)
4. Design and technology sports. (Homonyms, past participles)
5. Science and electricity. Traditional costumes. Value for money. (Adjective order, prefixes)
6. Keeping an open mind. History. (Synonyms, ed and ing adjectives)

pro_course_detail.title: Level Four
pro_course_detail.description:
1.Travel and communication. (Comparisons er - than, using adverbs of degree)

4. You are what your eat. (Future intentions, might)

Students MUST have a reasonably good prior knowledge of English.

Please do not select a 60 minute lesson for the 1st one. 30 minute lessons are exactly half the price of 60 minute ones and it gives me a chance to assess you.

Lesson formats will usually be as follows, UNLESS YOU WISH TO CONCENTRATE ON YOUR OWN TOPICS, (in which case a bespoke package will be built for you).

Students will be sent an article which will be discussed in the lesson. 

They read the article and mark any words or phrases they do not understand in Red. 

They then find definitions which they put after the words or phrases in English. Any words or phrases they still do not understand they change to green.

The article is discussed thoroughly during the lesson, questions asked both ways and opinions sought.

This allows the student to Read, Write, Listen, Comprehend and Increase Vocabulary in one lesson.

Brazil’s history is full of fascinating stories. I’ll guide you through major events and show you how to talk about them naturally in Portuguese. Whether it’s colonization, independence, or modern-day movements, we’ll make history come to life.

If you’re interested in the romantic side of Brazilian culture, I can help you learn the language of dating! From flirting to understanding cultural norms, you’ll feel more confident in expressing yourself and connecting with others.

Vocabulary Building: Learn essential words and expressions for common situations, such as meeting new people, talking about your family, or describing your day.

Grammar Basics: We’ll cover the foundational grammar you need, such as simple verb tenses (present, past), articles, and basic sentence structure.

Pronunciation Practice: I’ll help you pronounce key words and sounds correctly, focusing on clear communication.

Interactive Activities: Fun, hands-on exercises to help reinforce what you’ve learned, like practicing dialogues, matching exercises, or simple Q&A.

Who This Lesson Is For:

Beginners (A1) who are starting to learn English and want to build a strong foundation.

Students looking for simple, easy-to-understand lessons that introduce them to essential vocabulary and grammar.

Those who prefer learning in a relaxed, supportive environment with practical, everyday language.

Materials:

Simple dialogues and vocabulary lists that are appropriate for beginner learners.

No textbooks needed—just a desire to learn and speak English!earn and communicate!
